newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Demirel addresses new parliament session.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Demirel addresses new parliament session.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel reaffirmed Turkey's secular foundations on Tuesday in an address at the start of a new parliament session following a two-month summer recess.
"The Turkish Republic will remain a democratic, secular and social consitutional state," Demirel told parliament.
In his speech to the 550-seat assembly, Demirel issued a warning against "countries supporting terrorism" in the region.
"I want to warn countries continuing to support terrorism in our region once more. Enmity against Turkey will only bring you harm," he said.
Turkey says Kurdish rebels fighting for independence or autonomy in the southeast of the country receive support in neighbouring countries Syria, Iraq and Iran.
The main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) has promised to toughen its criticism of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist-led coalition government in the months ahead.
ANAP leaders met at a mountain resort in western Turkey at the weekend to draw up a plan to bring down the three-month-old coalition through censure motions against ministers.
The alliance of Erbakan's Welfare Party with the conservative True Path Party of pro-West Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller has 279 MPs, four more than the number needed to defeat a censure motion.
The government also has the tepid backing of seven deputies from a small far-right group.
